the_publication_lag_the_operator_asked_t.the_fact: FINRA publishes the daily CNMS Reg SHO short-volume file AFTER the 16:00 ET close. Measured for 2026 only: Last-Modified 1.30-1.31 hours after the close, about 17:18 ET on session s, in 34 of 34 owned files.
the_publication_lag_the_operator_asked_t.why: The file for session s does not exist at the close of s, so a decision timestamped at the close of s may not read it. A decision made after the close of session s+1 may use files up to and including session s; entry at the open of s+2. A zero-lag rule would read a file published after the decision instant, which is leakage.
the_publication_lag_the_operator_asked_t.why_not_tighter: The 17:18 ET posting time is MEASURED FOR 2026 ONLY. The certification states that FINRA's historical posting time is NOT ESTABLISHED for any earlier year and that the Last-Modified header of a back-fetched old file is not evidence of its original posting instant. A lag justified by a posting time nobody observed in the sample years is an assumption wearing a measurement's clothes.

For the same reason the director ran NO network reachability probe against FINRA's archive: no depth measurement can move a mechanism refusal, and measuring it would create the appearance of a live path that does not exist.
